text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Reconstruction and Development Minister Jure Radic announces the rebuilding of 4,000 homes during 1997.
- Croatian Social-Liberal Party leader Vlado Gotovac rumoured to be considering backing out of the presidential race.
- U.S. Ambassador to Croatia Peter Galbraith says Croatia's integration into European structures hinges on allowing minority Serbs to return to their homes.
- The Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development issues 700 million Austrian schilling Eurobond after signing an agreement with 13 foreign banks.
- A secret makeshift tunnel linking the western and the eastern sections of Mostar discovered by western Mostar construction workers.
- The state securities commission gives a green light for 14 firms and banks to issue new shares.
- Industrial output in April rises by 6.5 percent compared to the same month of 1996, with January-April output rise at a lower 3.7 percent.
- Economic reintegration of Eastern Slavonia starts slowly with goods transactions. Public companies break the ice by reopening in the region.
- UN Human Rights rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn forwards a letter to Foreign Minister Mate Granic demanding that Serbs in Croatia be guaranteed their full rights.
- We will punish monopoly manipulations, says Desa Mlikotin Tomic, head of the Agency for the Protection of Market Competition, in an interview.
- Stock Exchange: Trade up 1.3 times last week compared to a week earlier, but stock prices mostly lower. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
